title: Odisha Bans Sea Fishing and Tourist Entry as Cyclone Arnab Nears October 28 Landfall
excerpt: Fishing is completely prohibited and hills, waterfalls and dams are closed to tourists in Odisha's vulnerable southern districts, with schools shut October 28-29 and 30 response teams deployed.
body:
• Odisha has completely prohibited sea fishing and banned tourist entry to hills, waterfalls, dams and scenic destinations in the vulnerable southern districts ahead of Cyclone Arnab's expected October 28 landfall.
  • The Hindu reports resources mobilised in six southern districts — Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur — while the state deployment covers five most vulnerable districts with 24 ODRAF and 6 NDRF teams.
  • Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five most vulnerable districts will stay closed on October 28 and 29, and leave for district officers has been cancelled with 24/7 control rooms activated.
  • If you have family in southern Odisha, tell them to follow district advisories, avoid coastal and hill destinations, and expect evacuations from kutcha houses and low-lying areas to cyclone shelters.

Odisha has banned fishing in the sea and closed tourist destinations across its vulnerable southern districts, tightening precautions two days before Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall on October 28. The new restrictions — reported by The Hindu and detailed in state reporting by Sambad English — go beyond the red alert and disaster deployment the state announced earlier this week.

What Is New: Fishing and Tourist Bans

Fishing activities in the sea have been completely prohibited as a precautionary measure. Tourist entry to hills, waterfalls, dams and scenic destinations has also been banned across the vulnerable districts. The Hindu said the government has mobilised its resources in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur, the identified vulnerable districts of the southern region. The state's detailed deployment, reported by Sambad English and Odisha Ray, names five districts as most vulnerable — Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri — where the tourist ban, school closures and response teams are concentrated.

Farmers have been advised by the Agriculture Department to harvest and safely store paddy, maize, ragi and other crops that have reached 80 to 85 percent maturity, with dedicated agricultural helplines opened for assistance.

Teams, Shelters and Closures Already in Place

A total of 30 response teams have been positioned: 24 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams and six National Disaster Response Force teams. Ganjam, considered particularly vulnerable, has nine ODRAF and two NDRF teams; Gajapati has six ODRAF and one NDRF team; and Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri have three ODRAF and one NDRF team each.

Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five most vulnerable districts will remain closed on Wednesday, October 28 and Thursday, October 29. Leave for district-level officers and staff has been cancelled, officials have been told to remain at headquarters, and round-the-clock control rooms are operating at district, block, tehsil and urban local body levels, with helpline and toll-free numbers available.

District administrations are identifying residents in kutcha houses, thatched huts and low-lying areas for relocation to cyclone shelters stocked with essential amenities, under the state's zero-casualty objective. Expectant mothers near their delivery dates are being shifted in advance to community health centres, primary health centres and hospitals, with special arrangements for senior citizens, children and persons with disabilities.

Health, Power and Livestock Measures

Health authorities have been directed to stock essential medicines, including snake antivenom and chlorine tablets, and to arrange water chlorination to reduce the risk of waterborne disease. Equipment for restoring power and telecommunications has been pre-positioned for quick restoration if services are disrupted. For livestock, the measures include moving animals to safer locations, treatment through Mobile Veterinary Units and distribution of cattle feed and fodder in vulnerable pockets, according to Odisha Ray's account of the state preparations.

What Happens Next

The India Meteorological Department expects the cyclone to make landfall between southern Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh on October 28, with a higher probability of crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast, bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall and strong winds to southern Odisha. Nodal officers have been assigned to vulnerable sectors and linked through dedicated WhatsApp groups for real-time reporting. The government has urged residents to ignore rumours, follow official advisories and cooperate with local administrations as the system approaches. No end date for the fishing and tourist bans was announced in the reports; they are precautionary measures tied to the landfall window.
